doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Squirrel Nut Zippers and the swing revival
summary: Pallo played concerts with the Squirrel Nut Zippers, learning songs by ear, and recalls the swing revival at Roseland.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: I did a few concerts with them and that was different too. They did all original songs and I never rehearsed with them and I did one, two, — one was at Roseland, I did a show with them at Roseland, a New Year’s Eve party in Washington, DC, I can’t think of the name of the place. And they would call me and say, “Come on, we want you on the show.” I would listen to the first chorus to hear where the changes went, and I would play very soft. I knew what key they were in, and then now I nailed in. The second chorus I’m right with them.
But I had no idea, because it was all original songs that they did. But it was fun working with them.
Yeah, I think they must have broken up by now.
Yeah there was a — I forget how many years ago
There seemed to be like this “Swing’s Back.” LP Swing’s back, right.
It wasn’t back for too long.

It wasn’t back — you’re right. But it was cute though, at Roseland I recall seeing these young kids — I say young kids — young people dancing to jitterbug and things like that and they had the 1940s dresses on and zoot suits and all that stuff, and they were dancing and we’re playing up there and oh it was great. But it didn’t come back too long like you said. But today of course you have the rap stuff.
